title: The God Who Brought You Out

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I am the LORD, who brought you up out of Egypt to be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy." - Lev 11:45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One sentence, and it holds the whole logic of the Christian life.

First, the rescue: I am the LORD, who brought you up out of Egypt. That happened before a single law was given. Israel did not earn their freedom by good behaviour. They were slaves, powerless, and God came down and brought them out.

Second, the purpose: to be your God. He did not rescue them and then leave them to themselves. He rescued them for relationship.

Third, the response: therefore be holy. Not "so that" — therefore. Holiness is the natural shape of a rescued life.

Every believer has an Egypt. Whatever held you — sin, shame, addiction, self-righteousness, despair — you did not free yourself. Christ came down into the darkness, bore your sin at the cross, and brought you out at the cost of His own blood (Col 1:13-14).

So when Scripture calls you to holiness, it is never a demand from a distant God testing whether you qualify. It is the loving call of the One who has already rescued you, saying: live like the free person you now are. You do not go back to Egypt. You belong to Me.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What was the "Egypt" God brought you out of?
2. Do you ever live as though you are still enslaved to it?
3. How does remembering your rescue fuel your obedience today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for coming down into my Egypt and bringing me out at the cost of Your Son. Let the memory of that rescue shape everything about how I live today. Amen.
